title: Hardware-aware quant/profile publisher + pin retry & rollback process for model onboarding
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Formalize an automated publisher and rollback process for hardware-specific performance profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) that includes quantization variants, signature versioning, and an automatic pin retry/decay workflow for model onboarding. This ticket covers the end-to-end flow: micro-bench harness outputs -> profile generation -> validation gates -> publish to catalog -> auto-pin heuristics for customers and canary rollout + deterministic rollback rules.

Background: We already collect device-level microbenchmarks during onboarding, but publishing is manual and pins are sometimes applied too aggressively. This results in customer applications getting surprised when a later minor kernel change makes a pinned variant slower (observed regressions on L40S 2048-seq workload). We need: a) deterministic performance signatures per HW variant and quant profile, b) TTL/decay and retry policies for pins, c) publish metadata that includes confidence and failure-mode guidance, d) an operational runbook + automated checks for publishers.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope includes generator, validator, publisher, and rollback rules.
- Does NOT include UI changes to Console (separate PM ticket).
- Does NOT include new hardware acquisition or low-level kernel work.

Key decisions (proposal):
1) Signature model: Publish a compressed signature file per model/version/quant/hw that contains: sample latency p50/p95/p99 at target sequences, throughput at target batch sizes, memory headroom, and a small set of representative generated traces for QA. The signature will be a stable artifact (SHA256) with semantic versioning: v{major}.{minor}.{patch}-hw.{variant}. Example: v1.3.0-hw.A100.
2) Confidence scoring: Each signature gets a confidence score (0-100) computed from sample variance, number of runs, and cross-device agreement. >85 is high confidence. Profiles with <60 cannot be auto-pinned.
3) Auto-pin heuristic: Auto-pin only when: signature.confidence>=85 AND latency p95 delta to baseline <= +10% AND throughput >= baseline * 0.9. Otherwise suggest pin or create a conditional pin (canary 5% traffic).
4) Pin TTL & decay: Pins created by the auto-publisher have a TTL of 30 days. TTL auto-extends if signatures from subsequent calibrations stay within drift thresholds; otherwise pin enters a 'stale' state and is eligible for automated retry or safe-unpin.
5) Pin retry/backoff: If a pinned variant fails validation in production (observed customer error spike or latency regression beyond thresholds), the system will: a) revert traffic to fallback variant, b) mark the pinned signature as suspect and schedule a re-calibration job with exponential backoff (1d, 3d, 7d) up to 3 attempts. After failures, the profile is demoted and the publisher receives an alert.
6) Rollback rules: Deterministic rollback contract: if customer_{95th}_latency > pinned_signature_{95th} * 1.25 OR error_rate increases by >200% relative to baseline in a 30-minute window, trigger immediate rollback and run validation pipeline.

Deliverables:
- Signature generator script integrated into onboarding harness (CI).
- Validator that runs a set of smoke tests across A100/H100/L40S/MI300 and emits a confidence score.
- Publisher that writes profiles to model-catalog with metadata, TTL, semantic versioning, and can trigger auto-pin per heuristic.
- Pin manager service that implements TTL, decay, retry/backoff, demotion, and rollback hooks.
- Runbook for on-call + paging rules and a dashboard link.

Acceptance criteria:
- The signature generator produces repeatable artifacts (SHA256 stable) for 4 representative models used in onboarding (small/medium/large/llm).
- The validator computes confidence and rejects low confidence signatures for auto-pinning.
- Auto-pin heuristic runs in the staging publisher and pins a test model to A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants (canary mode) without manual intervention.
- Pin TTL and retry logic execute in simulated failures in our integration test harness.
- Runbook documented with steps for manual rollback, triage checklist, and postmortem template.

Note on metrics used for thresholds: thresholds chosen to balance stability for customer apps versus allowing higher-throughput quant variants. We expect to tune after 2 weeks of canaries across internal traffic and 1–2 pilot customers.
acceptance_criteria: Signature artifacts produced for each HW variant with stable SHA256 and semantic version metadata
Validator rejects signatures with confidence < 60 for auto-pinning
Auto-publisher can apply a conditional canary pin (5% traffic) when heuristic shows moderate gains
Pin manager enforces TTL (30d) and backs off retries on repeated calibration failures
Rollback triggers automatically for 95th-latency delta > 25% or error-rate spike > 200% and reverts traffic to fallback variant
tasks: Instrument microbench harness to emit signature JSON and SHA256 (ENG-1)
Publisher: metadata schema, semantic versioning, and catalog write API (ENG-3)
Pin manager: TTL, decay, retry/backoff, demotion, and rollback hooks (ENG-4)
Integration tests simulating latency and error spikes (ENG-5)
Docs + Confluence page linking the publisher contract and examples (ENG-7)
